sources.role: pinned Retro8 core, libretro input descriptors and serialization implementation
official project scope and desktop/libretro build description

linux.reason: Retro8 is a libretro core with runtime joypad callbacks; the pinned core owns neither the RetroArch host paths nor a persistent controller, save, state, firmware, or key namespace.
evidence: source:src/libretro/libretro.cpp retro_serialize_size returns 0 and serialize/unserialize are stubs @ddc06a14

linux-flatpak.reason: The pinned repository provides libretro and desktop build files but no Retro8 Flatpak manifest or verified Flatpak package.
evidence: source:README.md describes compilation and RetroArch-core use but no Flatpak target @ddc06a14
source:repository tree contains no Flatpak manifest @ddc06a14

windows.reason: The repository includes a Windows SDL project and a libretro core, but neither establishes a persistent host-controller grammar or core-owned save/state/firmware paths.
evidence: source:projects/vs2017/retro8/retro8.vcxproj and src/config.h PLATFORM_WIN32 fixed SDL keyboard defaults @ddc06a14

macos.reason: The repository contains an Xcode project, but the libretro core still delegates host controller/configuration and persistence to its frontend; no stable Retro8-owned macOS path grammar is published.
evidence: source:src/libretro/libretro.cpp runtime joypad callbacks and zero-size serialization @ddc06a14

controller_boundary.refusal: Do not invent a Retro8 controller profile: the pinned libretro core exposes runtime RetroPad callbacks but no persistent host-controller mapping grammar; RetroArch configuration and device profiles are frontend-owned.

notes: Retro8 is an open-source PICO-8 reimplementation/core. The core reports p8/png content and fixed runtime descriptors, but does not implement serialized state or external BIOS/key loading. RetroArch frontend runtime and package behavior were not verified.
